name: Baseball Poker
description: Baseball Poker is a raucous, high-action variant of 7-Card Stud that incorporates the rules and terminology of America's pastime. By designating 3s and 9s as wild cards and allowing 4s to trigger 'extra bases' (additional cards), the game dramatically increases the typical poker hand power. It is a quintessential 'Kitchen Table' poker game, favored for its massive pots and the chaos of players holding 8 or 9 cards in a showdown.

history.origins: Emerging in the mid-20th century in the United States, Baseball Poker was one of the first popular thematic poker variants. It was designed to maximize 'action' and excitement in home games, where players grew bored of the math-heavy constraints of standard Stud.
timeline: 1940s: 7-Card Stud becomes the dominant parlor poker format.
1950s: The 'Baseball' theme is added, using 3, 4, and 9 based on baseball stats.
1970s: Becomes a staple of 'Dealer's Choice' nights.
Present: Frequently featured in 'Dealer's Choice' mixed games in both home and legal card rooms (with special house rules).
history.cultural: Reflects the mid-century American obsession with baseball, turning the game's statistics into mathematical wild cards.
history.evolution: The game evolved into 'Night Baseball' or 'Blind Baseball', where all cards are dealt face down and players flip them one by one to resolve betting.

setup.players: 2-6 players (any more and the deck will run out due to extra cards).
setup.dealing: Standard 7-Card Stud pattern: Two cards down (hole), one up (the door card). Then three more upcards, and a final downcard.

rules.objective: Win the pot by having the highest 5-card poker hand at the showdown, or by forcing all other players to fold.
rules.gameplay: Baseball Poker proceeds through deal, legal play actions, and end-of-round resolution. Play proceeds through legal actions until round resolution.
keyRules: 3 face up = Match the pot or fold.
Best 5-card hand from the player's pool wins.

strategy.basic: Don't get attached to a pair of Aces. In Baseball, 'Three of a Kind' is a weak hand. You should be aiming for a Full House or better as a starting goal.
strategy.intermediate: The Four Advantage: If you get an extra card from a 4, you have a massive statistical advantage. You have many more ways to connect with the 3s and 9s in the deck.
strategy.advanced: Pot Match Bluffing: If someone matches the pot on a face-up 3, they are signaling 'I have a great hand' or 'I am pot-committed'. Use this to gauge whether to continue against them.
tips: Track the 3s and 9s showing on the board. If four of them are visible, the value of 'fishing' for a wild card drops significantly.
In a 6-player game, be aware of the deck size. If multiple players have 4s, the dealer may draw from the 'muck' or use a community card for the final downcard.

variations.name: Night Baseball
variations.description: All cards are dealt face down. Players turn cards over one at a time and bet. If you flip a 3, you're out (or match pot).
variations.emptyOverridesReason: Variation differences are described in rules text; engine overrides are not modeled separately.

variations.name: Baseball Lowball
variations.description: The LOWEST hand wins. 3s and 9s are wild but used to create the lowest possible total.
variations.emptyOverridesReason: Lowball scoring uses the same engine structure; only the ranking evaluation differs conceptually.

synthesis.shortDescription: Step up to the plate with the ultimate wild-card poker variant. Baseball Poker turns every hand into a high-scoring inning where 3s and 9s can be anything you need. Navigate the risk of the 'Matching Pot' and use your 'Extra Base' fours to build an unbeatable Five of a Kind.
